gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 24?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 24 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent real-time observations from Munich-area stations and consensus from numerical weather models, including GFS runs, show surface temperatures peaking near 24 °C during the afternoon under mostly cloudy skies, moderate easterly flow, and dew points in the low teens °C. This aligns closely with the long-term August 24 climatological normal of 23.4 °C and explains the market’s near-certain pricing on that exact outcome. A modest diurnal range, limited insolation from cloud cover, and absence of strong warm advection have kept readings from exceeding or falling short of this threshold. Only an unexpected late-day clearing combined with stronger southerly winds or a localized station-specific anomaly could realistically shift the official daily maximum away from 24 °C before midnight.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from sources including GFS ensembles and European agencies project a daytime high near 22–23°C in Munich on August 25 under light winds, with possible early sprinkles and overcast conditions. These factors limit peak solar heating and favor slightly lower maxima around 19–20°C, aligning with the closely matched market-implied probabilities for those outcomes. Late-August climatology shows typical highs of 21–23°C, but reduced insolation from clouds can suppress temperatures by 1–3°C compared to clear-sky scenarios. Model spread and timing of any precipitation introduce genuine uncertainty, keeping trader consensus balanced between the leading bins while assigning lower odds to 21°C or warmer. Updated model runs and official DWD guidance ahead of resolution will refine the exact threshold.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the UK Met Office and other models points to a daytime maximum of 24–25°C in London on August 25, 2026, under largely settled conditions with sunny spells and light easterly or northeasterly winds.** 

Early morning readings near 16–17°C at stations such as Heathrow have been followed by steady daytime heating under mostly clear skies and low precipitation risk (<10–20% in afternoon hours). This aligns with above-average August conditions but well below recent heatwave peaks earlier in the month. 

Model runs show limited spread, with peak values hinging on exact cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing; slight differences in insolation or a brief increase in low-level moisture could tip the official high between 24°C and 25°C. The market-implied odds (24°C at 59%, 25°C at 31.5%) reflect this narrow uncertainty band and the “wisdom of crowds” assessment of real-time observational data releases, with lower probabilities assigned to cooler or warmer outliers given the stable high-pressure influence and absence of significant frontal activity. 

Upcoming Met Office updates and hourly station reports through the afternoon will provide the final resolution criteria.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models points to a maximum temperature of 33–35°C in Tokyo on August 26, supporting the near-even market split between those outcomes. Persistent summer high pressure and southerly flow have maintained recent daily highs near 33–35°C, yet increasing mid-level moisture and a 20–40% chance of scattered afternoon showers or cloud build-up could cap peak readings by 1–2°C. Model runs diverge on timing and coverage of convection, creating the close implied probabilities around the 34°C and 35°C thresholds while historical August averages near 31°C underscore the current elevated baseline. Updated JMA guidance and next model cycles will refine resolution criteria for the daily maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover and morning showers across Munich on August 25 are capping daytime heating, keeping the daily maximum near 19–21 °C and driving the near-even market split between 19 °C and 20 °C. Light westerly flow and high humidity further limit surface warming while scattered precipitation enhances evaporative cooling. Official guidance from the German Weather Service and GFS ensembles shows only modest afternoon clearing, with any breaks in the overcast offering the main pathway for a brief spike toward 21–22 °C. Traders are therefore weighting the likelihood of sustained stratus and rain-cooled air, which historically suppresses late-August maxima by 2–3 °C relative to clear-sky potential.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 24 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
